claims.text: A machine-learning-based interatomic potential can represent atomic configurations in ab initio liquids of multicomponent high-entropy alloys more accurately than TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The new potential will improve the representation of atomic interactions and configurations.
Capturing complex interactions more accurately will improve reference-target phase-space overlap.
Improved reference-target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The intervention is applicable to equiatomic and non-equiatomic mixtures containing three to six principal elements.
The intervention is applicable from 0.8 to 1.2 times the alloy melting temperature.
The intervention applies to both solid and liquid states at or near high melting temperatures.
The new potential will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by at least 30% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed 30% improvement corresponds to reducing free-energy error from 10 meV/atom to 7 meV/atom.
The accuracy of the new potential may depend on training-data quality and implementation details.
The proposed benchmark compares free-energy errors from the new potential and TOR-TILD's EAM references against ab initio calculations for a set of high-entropy alloys.
The hypothesis is to be falsified if the new potential fails to reduce free-energy error by at least 20% for at least 80% of the benchmark alloys.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires at least a 30% reduction, whereas the stated falsification rule accepts a 20% reduction for 80% of alloys. Thus, results below the prediction, such as a 25% reduction across all alloys, would contradict the quantitative hypothesis but would not falsify it under the stated rule.
